Weighed against filing this as blocking: the same slide has been through two deliberate Antti-directed trims (2026-08-25, 2026-08-29) that explicitly cut an output-preview/interpretive line for lean-slide reasons, and re-adding rescue text without also re-litigating mode-agnostic wording (the keystroke itself was cut on purpose) is a real editorial trade-off, not an oversight a mechanical fix corrects. Reporting as a TODO for the maintainer rather than a blocking finding: the fix is not obvious enough to prescribe without their call.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Preamble before action — design around it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the CURRENT (2026-09-03-narrowed) rule guards against: for a plan-mode-flagged prompt specifically, Claude's preamble can eat the top-of-response slot before the load-bearing content appears, and the rule now makes suppression MANDATORY (not advisory) for every plan-mode prompt, dropping the old 4+-step trigger this one-clause prompt would have escaped under. This prompt's frontmatter declares `permission-mode: plan` (curriculum/prompts/when-a-plan-is-good-1.md), and neither required form is present: the fence has no in-fence 'No preamble. <first action>' suppressor as its last line, and the body carries no primer after the fence naming preamble + a skim-past cue. The maintainer block itself shows the file once had exactly this kind of primer and cut it on purpose: L59 lists 'the output-preview line ("Watch what comes back. Sometimes Claude names the read-only state…")' among the content deliberately removed 2026-08-29, a full week before the rule's 2026-09-03 narrowing made a primer mandatory here. Weighed against filing this blocking: the prompt is a self-reflective diagnostic question, not a task-execution or plan-generation prompt, so there is no separable 'plan payload' behind a throwaway preamble for the rule's harm to protect -- the entire response, preamble included, is the observation the exercise wants read. That weakens but doesn't erase the drifted rule's literal mandate, so this is reported as a TODO / rule question rather than blocked: either the rule should carve out reflective/self-report prompts from the plan-mode-ONLY trigger, or the maintainer adds the one-line primer back.
